notes: The 10-year US interest rate (5.28%) is 1.28% above the 3-month rate (3.99%), and that gap has widened by 0.49% in 3 months: often a sign that growth is picking up.
Copper has gained 6.1% on gold over 3 months. Copper follows factory and building demand, while gold is bought in worrying times, so this points to stronger growth.
Oil is down 18% in 6 months: lower costs for businesses, but often a sign of weaker demand.
Fear gauge (VIX) at 15.3: markets are calm (under 16 = calm, over 25 = stressed).
The US stock market (S&P 500) is above its average price over the last 200 trading days (about 10 months): its long-term uptrend is intact.

todaysConditions.note: Oil is up 33% over 3 months: a boost for markets full of oil and gas companies, and a cost for countries that import a lot of oil.

The fear gauge (VIX) is a calm 15.3 (18 or less), and world stocks are 6.1% above their average price over the last 200 trading days (about 10 months). When investors feel confident, emerging markets usually benefit.
